drivers.lead: Dixon's six span seventeen seasons, from 2003 to 2020, and they are the record for the IndyCar Series era
drivers.note: The word era is doing work there. These records begin in 1996, the first season of the Indy Racing League, and on that basis Scott Dixon leads. All-time he is second: A. J. Foyt won seven national championships between 1960 and 1979, in the AAA and USAC lineage the modern series counts as its own, and Dixon has been one short since 2020. None of his six are consecutive — 2003, 2008, 2013, 2015, 2018 and 2020, spread about as evenly across a career as it is possible to be — and the 2015 one was settled on a tiebreaker, tied on points with Juan Pablo Montoya and decided three wins to two. The pressure now comes from Palou, whose four in five seasons include three straight from 2023. Dario Franchitti also has four, and nobody else in this window has more than three.
